report.summary: Mostly sound. The test now waits on a gate instead of sleeping, the R2 put failure is limited to this test's own key, and the Dockerfile chmod fixes non-root access to /opt/tempo/pi/tempo-profile.ts. One likely blocker: ops.test.ts now calls Promise.withResolvers, which is only typed in lib ES2024 or later, but apps/tempo/tsconfig.json sets lib ES2023 and includes test/. This should break `bun run typecheck` (CLAUDE.md rule 15). I could not run tsc to confirm: node_modules is outside the directories I can reach and the shell blocked a scratch tsc probe.

findings.text: Promise.withResolvers is not in the ES2023 lib that apps/tempo/tsconfig.json uses, and this test file is in that config's include list. No local declaration adds it (grep of the repo and of worker-runtime.d.ts found none), so tsc should report TS2550 and `bun run typecheck` should fail. Fix: build the gate with new Promise and a captured resolve function, or raise lib to ES2024. Running `bun run typecheck` at the head commit would confirm.

evidence.why: apps/tempo/tsconfig.json has `"lib": ["ES2023", "DOM", "DOM.Iterable"],` and includes "test". TypeScript declares PromiseConstructor.withResolvers only in lib.es2024.promise.d.ts. Nothing else in the repo uses withResolvers or mentions ES2024, and the generated worker-runtime.d.ts does not declare it, so this line should not type-check. CLAUDE.md requires `bun run typecheck` to pass.

checked.risk: Tests: sleeps or timing assertions, shared spies under concurrency, assertions that can pass vacuously
Build: typecheck config covers the changed test code
Build and runtime environment: file modes and the user that runs processes in the image
Spec: pi extension path and loading by the tempo user

Failure paths, idempotency, security, real contracts: the change touches only tests and one permission line, so none applies beyond the R2 put spy, which passes all other calls through to the real put
